Milestone 7.9 · Fleet Remaster · Batch closeout

11 units, rebuilt through Meshy — before and after

Every unit in the fleet was regenerated with a brighter de-lit albedo to kill the wash-out. This page answers two questions per unit: is the wash-out gone, and does the result match its approved concept — judged against fresh in-engine captures taken in L_Arena under its real sun. Each unit was committed separately so it can be reverted on its own.

branch main HEAD 6bd1cee origin/main ca5c127 — 15 behind pushed no 12 commits 11 units + 1 fix

Incident — files I destroyed during this audit

While dry-running the revert checks I ran a command whose && chain broke: the throwaway worktree was never created, so the cleanup statements after it executed against the real working tree — git reset --hard HEAD and git clean -fd. This was my error, not a pipeline fault.

  • LOSTThe in-engine verify screenshots — all .claude/pipeline/handoffs/TASK-3NN-verify-<Unit>-{tight,threequarter,wide,feet}.png. They were untracked and not ignored, so git clean -fd deleted them permanently. They were never committed, so Git cannot restore them. They have since been re-captured (2026-07-26) and are committed to Git, so this exposure is closed — every "in-engine" cell below is a fresh capture, not a stand-in.
  • LOSTUncommitted edits to TASKBOARD.md — the file now matches HEAD exactly. The manager was writing the board at the time, so its in-progress work needs redoing.
  • INTACTAll 12 commits and origin/main. HEAD never moved — the reflog shows reset: moving to 6bd1cee, the same commit — and nothing was pushed.
  • INTACTCONVENTIONS.md, BP_Unit_Footman.uasset, L_Arena.umap, pipeline_manifest.json — still dirty, as expected. The Unreal Editor held file locks on the .uasset/.umap files, which made the unlink fail and saved them.
  • INTACTAll Content/RawAssets/ art. These are Git-LFS files; their on-disk mtimes are still the artist's run times and their content matches the commits.

Resolved. All 44 verify shots (plus two extra evidence shots) were re-captured in Simulate on 2026-07-26 and committed, so they can no longer be lost to a working-tree command.

Every commit is scoped to its own unit. None of the known-dirty files (CONVENTIONS.md, TASKBOARD.md, BP_Unit_Footman.uasset, L_Arena.umap, pipeline_manifest.json) was swept into any of them — with one deliberate exception: Footman's d7254da carries pipeline_manifest.json, and the diff is only the Footman albedo_delight block that became the fleet-wide brightness profile. That is in-scope for the pilot, not a foreign sweep.

MilitiaMob is the one unit that is not independently revertible. 6bd1cee later rewrote five of the same binary .uasset files, so reverting f14f325 on its own conflicts. To back MilitiaMob out, revert the pair newest-first: git revert --no-commit 6bd1cee f14f325.

How to read each unit

before — the albedo that was shipped after — the albedo shipped now bar scale: mean-linear luminance, 0 → 0.40 higher = brighter base colour = less wash-out

Each unit shows two rows. Row 1 — provenance: the concept art it was generated against, then the real albedo texture files pulled straight out of Git LFS at the commit before and the commit after that unit's remaster — not reconstructions. Row 2 — in-engine: screenshots taken in the Unreal editor in Simulate, in L_Arena under its actual directional sun, on 2026-07-26. These are raw viewport captures — centre-cropped and scaled only, with no colour grading. The Blender/Cycles turntable previews that previously stood in for them have been removed; the only Cycles image left on the page is Footman's genuine pre-remaster render, kept as the one real before-render and labelled as such.

Open items for Jonathan

  1. Verify screenshots: re-captured and committed. All 11 units × 4 shots were re-shot in Simulate under L_Arena's sun on 2026-07-26 and are now tracked in Git, so the earlier loss cannot repeat. Two extra evidence shots were added for the open questions below: TASK-318-verify-Pikeman-rank.png and TASK-319-verify-Cavalry-gait.png. Grounding measured at capture time: 2.15–2.40 cm float on every unit, matching TASK-308.
  2. The manager's TASKBOARD.md edits need redoing — I discarded them. I deliberately did not write the board myself, so none of my work is layered on top of the loss.
  3. Ogre is the weakest colour read in the fleet. Lowest post-remaster albedo (0.142) and the smallest team region at 1.33%, against the 2.1% that shipped. It goes pale under the arena sun. Wants either a brightness bump or a larger team region.
  4. Pikeman's pikes overhang the rank flanks — now shown directly in TASK-318-verify-Pikeman-rank.png: four Pikemen at the C++ capsule spacing (r40 → 80 cm) from the gameplay camera. The capture confirms the pike tips project past both outer men, and that it is the blue helmets and shoulder plates — not the shafts — that merge into a continuous blue band across the rank. Pikeman also carries the fleet's largest team region at 10.31%.
  5. Cavalry's gait is stiff and slides (TASK-233) — a side-on frame mid-*_Walk is now attached as TASK-319-verify-Cavalry-gait.png for judging it. It needs a quadruped animation source, and FAB-005/006 do not provide one, so it stays blocked until a source is chosen. Team colour also bleeds onto the horse's forehead.
  6. SM_MilitiaMob carries older geometry. The same-path reimport wedged its LOD chain, so 6bd1cee reverted the static mesh. Runtime is unaffected — SK_MilitiaMob is the runtime visual — but the static preview mesh is stale pending the manager's follow-up task.
  7. Cleric is the brightest unit at 0.361 and Knight's steel is deliberately dark. Both are called out so they are not mistaken for defects: Cleric's pale cream robe is faithful to its concept, and Knight's low final value is intended dark metal.
  8. Nothing is pushed. origin/main is still ca5c127, 15 commits behind. Pushing is your call alone.
